title: Natural quotient Hom comparison with the rank-one computation
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative ring, J an ideal, and U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Let F_n be the ordinary quotient module realization of [def-sfb-adic-perfect-module-functors], let G be constant A-module sections at the terminal object of the slice, with additive scalars forgotten, and set H_n = G composed with quotient by J^(n+1) from [def-sfb-adic-short-complex-quotient-tower]. There exist additive maps t_n(M,N):H_n(Hom_A(M,N)) to Hom(F_n M,F_n N) for arbitrary A-modules M,N. They are natural in arbitrary pre- and postcomposition, are bijective for M=A, and intertwine G of the canonical algebraic successor quotient transition with scalar change conjugated by the fixed ordinary balancing isomorphisms. Bijectivity for any other source module is not part of this statement.

source.place: Lemma lemma-connected-adic-lisse, Tag 09C6, quotient total-Hom calculation, its single-module finite-projective evaluation step; Modules on Sites Tag 093T; More on Algebra Tag 0A8H.

proof.text: Retain A-linear scalars on constant quotient sections H_n. Use the scalar section adjunction and normalization [lem-sfb-adic-perfect-quotient-section-adjunction] to obtain F_n left adjoint to R_n, an isomorphism e_n:H_n to F_n R_n, and the successor section insertion kappa with its unit and quotient-transition identities.

Define ev_m:Hom_A(M,N) to N by evaluation. For x in H_n(Hom_A(M,N)), the assignment m maps to H_n(ev_m)(x) is A-linear because H_n is additive and A-linear. Postcompose by e_n(N), and transpose through the adjunction, to obtain t_n(M,N). The map is additive in x. Evaluation commutes with precomposition and postcomposition; functoriality, naturality of e_n, and naturality of the adjunction prove the required two-variable identity. The Lean proof supplies private proved evaluation and adjunction lemmas.

For M=A, ev_1:Hom_A(A,N) to N is an isomorphism, hence H_n(ev_1) is an isomorphism. Linear maps A to H_n(N) are determined by their value at 1, so x maps bijectively to the evaluation linear map. Postcomposition by e_n(N) and transposition through the adjunction are bijections. This proves the rank-one claim without any finite-projective internal-Hom theorem.

Naturality of the quotient section transition with each ev_m identifies the two evaluation maps. For a morphism f:F_(n+1)(M) to F_(n+1)(N), expand the transpose of theta_M inverse followed by change(f) followed by theta_N using the lower adjunction unit. Substitute the unit identity, cancel theta_M followed by its inverse, and use naturality of kappa. The result is the upper transpose followed by kappa and R_n(theta_N). Apply the section-transition identity to the evaluation map. Injectivity of the lower adjunction Hom equivalence gives exactly the stated successor formula. This is the proved successor_mate and adjointHomComparison_transition calculation.

theorem adicPerfectUnitHom (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X) :
    let G := AdicCohomology.sections
      ((coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X).over U) (Over.mk (𝟙 U)) ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat A) AddCommGrpCat
    let H := fun n : ℕ ↦ AdicCohomology.quotient J (n + 1) ⋙ G
    let F := fun n : ℕ ↦ adicPerfectQuotientFunctor X J U n
    ∃ t : ∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A),
        (H n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N)) →+ ((F n).obj M ⟶ (F n).obj N),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A),
        Function.Bijective (t n (ModuleCat.of A A) N)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M M' N N' : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A)
        (a : M' ⟶ M) (b : N ⟶ N') (x : (H n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))),
        t n M' N' ((H n).map (ModuleCat.ofHom
          ((LinearMap.llcomp A M' N N' b.hom).comp (LinearMap.lcomp A N a.hom))) x) =
          (F n).map a ≫ t n M N x ≫ (F n).map b) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A)
        (x : (H (n + 1)).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))),
        t n M N (G.map ((AdicCohomology.transition J
          (Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.le_succ n) 1)).app
            (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))) x) =
          ((adicPerfectQuotientModuleStep X J U n).app M).inv ≫
            (change (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep X J U n)).map (t (n + 1) M N x) ≫
              ((adicPerfectQuotientModuleStep X J U n).app N).hom)
